recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Future binding-strength changes or new substance terminology should wait for a new BRR/vocabulary decision because FHIR-31836 explicitly retained example strength for most substance-specific bindings pending more implementation experience.
issue_request: FHIR-31836 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked whether SubstanceSpecification coded elements such as name.type, name.domain, and relationship.type should have extensible or required bindings. The final resolution says all bindings were reviewed, value sets were created, a few were made required, and most binding strengths should remain example until more experience is gained.
initial_application: No commit explicitly naming FHIR-31836 was found. The apparent application was the broader January 2022 BRR/MedDef terminology work: c4105f29435c and related commits created substance code systems and value sets, 9ee11711505a added the SubstanceDefinition bindings, and later QA/metadata commits refined those terminology resources.
additional_context: SubstanceSpecification is represented in the current build as active SubstanceDefinition source. BRR minutes record FHIR-31836 as persuasive with value sets created and earlier grouped it with MedDef and Vocabulary work. Later FHIR-39596, already on the combined branch, intentionally left characterization.technique unbound after separating characterization from structure terminology, so that later element is not a missed FHIR-31836 application.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source change was needed because SubstanceDefinition.name.type, SubstanceDefinition.name.domain, and SubstanceDefinition.relationship.type already have example bindings to substance-name-type, substance-name-domain, and substance-relationship-type value sets, and the corresponding value set source files exist.
